1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing and short line lengths, though letter spacing looks standard rather than especially generous.

2.why: No italics, all-caps instruction text, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; only the codes themselves are uppercase, which is not instruction text.

3.why: The screenshots are desktop-width and show a narrow centred single-column card, so actual rendering at a mobile screen size cannot be confirmed from the evidence.

4.why: Every instruction is one or two short plain sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.'

5.why: The recovery-code field shows a format placeholder 'ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNPQ' and the demo box shows example email and mobile values, but the six-digit code fields themselves have no placeholder example.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two short sentences, so no long block of text must be read to proceed.

7.why: The setup secret and recovery codes are rendered as plain page text that can be selected and copied, but no copy button or explicit copy affordance is provided.

8.why: The app explicitly states 'A QR code is not required' and offers only manual entry of the 32-character secret, with no QR code or equivalent shown on any screen.

9.why: The fields are standard labelled inputs, but nothing in the screenshots demonstrates autocomplete attributes or password-manager support, so this cannot be confirmed.

10.why: Every screen has a large bold heading naming the current step and a single solid-blue primary button that clearly dominates the muted secondary buttons.

11.why: Each step presents one primary action (e.g. 'Verify identity', 'Activate MFA'), though secondary actions like 'Start again', 'Log out', and 'Generate new recovery codes' share the same screens.

12.why: Actions produce plain outcome messages such as 'Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.' and 'Your authenticator is ready for protected payments.', with each transition landing on a clearly titled next step.

13.why: A 'Start again' button, retry after errors, and regeneration of recovery codes are all offered without lockout, but no reveal/hide control exists and regenerating permanently invalidates previous codes.

14.why: The only observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming and says how to proceed, but it never states what the actual problem was.

15.why: The verification code 'expires in five minutes' and the authenticator code rotates every 30 seconds, so code entry is explicitly time-limited rather than generous, even though no reading countdown is shown.
